newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Abu Dhabi sets up $272 mln Islamic bank.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi sets up $272 mln Islamic bank.

text.p: Abu Dhabi on Wednesday issued a decree setting up Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank with capital of one billion dirhams, an official statement said.

It said the decree stipulated that the Abu Dhabi government would own 10 percent or 100 million dirhams of the new bank, the president's private office would have 50 million dirhams and the founders -- who were not named -- 240 million dirhams.
The rest would be offered to UAE nationals and the shares would have a nominal value of 10 dirhams each.
Islamic banks do not deal in interest -- the core of the Western banking system -- as it is regarded by many Moslems as usury, banned under Islamic sharia law.

Islamic banks have become more popular among the world's one billion Moslems, but the more than 185 financial institutions which strictly adhere to the principles of sharia law faced hurdles to lure more funds, bankers say.
